newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakura says has problems with Apollo rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Sakura says has problems with Apollo rescue plan.

text.p: Major Japanese commercial bank Sakura Bank Ltd said on Monday it would have trouble accepting a rehabilitation plan put forward by troubled loan firm Apollo Leasing Co.

Under the plan, Apollo is calling on creditors to waive 50 percent of their balance of loans, with remaining claims and debts to be written off by revenues from performing assets, a Sakura Bank spokesman said.
He said that the bank had told Apollo "it would be difficult to agree" on the restructuring plan. The spokesman did not make any further comment.

Apollo Leasing, a non-bank financial institution, extended loans to real estate firms during the bubble economy in the late 1980s. But like many small and medium-sized financial institutions, it was sent into a tailspin by the collapse of the asset-price bubble in the early 1990s.

As of end-March 1996, the balance of debt at the non-bank stood at 489.7 billion yen, Japanese media said at the weekend. Sakura Bank, one of Apollo's main creditors, has already written off most of the 82.7 billion yen owed to it by Apollo, they said.
The media reports said Sakura had rejected Apollo's proposed rehabilitation plan.
Apollo, which has more than 100 creditor financial institutions, also owes Nippon Credit Bank 69.3 billion yen, according to media reports.
